title: Day 719 — Sheinbaum Warns Against Foreign Intervention at Baja California Sur Accountability Stop; Governor Pledges Wetlands and Mangrove Protections
detail: On September 20, 2026 (Day 719, Sunday), President Sheinbaum held the next stop of her "Honestidad y Resultados" nationwide accountability tour in Baja California Sur, continuing the sovereignty message she struck a day earlier in Chihuahua. She told the crowd "México es un país libre, independiente y soberano, bastante nos costó" — invoking the historical cost in lives and sacrifice of Mexican independence — and argued that political authority rests with the Mexican people rather than with foreign powers or domestic elites seeking outside backing for internal disputes, a message read as a continued rebuttal to U.S. pressure narratives around cartel control and sovereignty. Baja California Sur Governor Víctor Manuel Castro Cosío used the event to announce a state commitment to protect the peninsula's wetlands, coastal dunes, mangroves, marine reefs and other protected natural areas from harmful development projects. Separately, border-area coverage noted Sheinbaum's motorcade had passed through Ciudad Juárez with her vehicle window down as residents gathered along the route, some chanting support, as she reiterated that defending national sovereignty and independence is a responsibility shared by all Mexicans.

media.caption: Sheinbaum warns against foreign intervention during her Baja California Sur accountability-tour stop

title: Day 719 — Sheinbaum Draws 50,000+ in Culiacán, Warns 'La Injerencia Provoca Violencia' Amid US Case Against Sinaloa Officials; Deploys Cabinet, Reviews Shrimp Imports
detail: On September 20, 2026 (Day 719, Sunday), President Sheinbaum led the Culiacán stop of her "Honestidad y Resultados en Sinaloa" accountability tour at the city's Feria Ganadera, drawing more than 50,000 attendees per state government figures. Addressing the fallout from the U.S. Justice Department's case against former governor Rubén Rocha Moya and other Sinaloa officials over alleged Sinaloa Cartel ties, Sheinbaum said "la injerencia no resuelve los problemas, la injerencia provoca violencia" and "no queremos injerencia de ningún gobierno extranjero en nuestro territorio," arguing the state's future must be decided by Sinaloans amid the ongoing Los Chapitos factional violence that intensified after Ismael "El Mayo" Zambada's July 2024 US capture. She reaffirmed federal backing for interim Governor Graciela Domínguez Nava (in office since Rocha Moya's indefinite leave began August 25) and said the Armed Forces would remain deployed in the state as long as necessary. Sheinbaum announced the federal cabinet will fan out across Sinaloa starting the following week for direct constituent attention: SADER pledged uninterrupted resources to farmers, CFE will extend electricity subsidies another month, SEP will build 20 new preparatory schools, SHCP will provide extraordinary budget support, and the ATDT's José Antonio Peña Merino will work with Customs to address producers' complaints about foreign (largely South American) shrimp undercutting Sinaloa's catch — "el mejor camarón es el de Sinaloa," she said. She cited roughly 94 billion pesos in federal investment in Sinaloa over two years spanning roads, ports, irrigation, health, housing and education, plus 1.128 million residents receiving welfare payments, 5,000 youths enrolled in "Jóvenes Unen al Barrio," 10 new community centers, a new Mazatlán vehicular bridge, 55,300 homes built, and over 400 free clinics under the Universal Health Service.

media.caption: More than 50,000 attend Sheinbaum's accountability-tour stop at the Culiacán Feria Ganadera
Sheinbaum warns that foreign interference provokes violence, addressing the US case against Sinaloa officials
Sheinbaum announces a review of foreign shrimp imports undercutting Sinaloa producers
